## Design

### 2026-11-03: I started planning the DicePopper. I did what I have done for all of the other projects and sketched up a design in a notebook. I also wrote a quick BOM on the other side. It is accurate to my project

**2h**

I started planning the DicePopper. I did what I have done for all of the other projects and sketched up a design in a notebook. I also wrote a quick BOM on the other side. It is accurate to my project except for information on solenoids. I couldn't find any available solenoids in NZ that use the right voltage/wattage, and are capable of popping up the plate.

![WIN_20261104_17_05_26_Pro](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6mG7f89ZDOsngQ8qn0yp6oxaSBtp0k8c/77fc6a190d52f92e453c526fedfb56760970b35133c38313d27530db2ed8d625.jpg)

![WIN_20261104_17_05_38_Pro](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6mG7f89ZDOsngQ8qn0yp6oxaSBtp0k8c/818c4c63aa857568752a97dabddb3d097c5bf061282b45f995e9a56aa578e280.jpg)

I have also been researching ways to lift and drop the plate effectively. I need it to use 5V and preferably not use many mechanical systems. I am considering using a few servo motors or a piston with a stepper. I am going to continue looking for options but I might start on other parts before I have decided. I found a cool website with mechanical systems and played around with them. It's called 507movements.com.

![Screenshot 2026-11-04 170947](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6mG7f89ZDOsngQ8qn0yp6oxaSBtp0k8c/2649b6f96674840e0140f2f640967411ede2d9edfd301e55088d233c8f540a59.png)

![Screenshot 2026-11-04 171144](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6mG7f89ZDOsngQ8qn0yp6oxaSBtp0k8c/310e6987d1b574a5bbbbfb4deb6c989391d961e909fa7fb14ec8282410ba3521.png)

### 2026-11-05: I designed the dice popper parts in Fusion360.

**6h**

I designed the dice popper parts in Fusion360.

![Screenshot 2026-11-04 180220](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6mG7f89ZDOsngQ8qn0yp6oxaSBtp0k8c/207806d842d92253ce4ee2a756e0725b649c19dc8880675f1e0eb37ad30f3035.png)

![Screenshot 2026-11-05 162213](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6mG7f89ZDOsngQ8qn0yp6oxaSBtp0k8c/cf1bd681d2ad27d0601759071ce8fb562f2ef409305a4f851f7c4731e19838f8.png)

![Screenshot 2026-11-05 162650](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6mG7f89ZDOsngQ8qn0yp6oxaSBtp0k8c/2cfcb44b3ac2f22d72fba34d3f278e0ad8b3cd5605bf35d127b6f391e067aefb.png)

![Screenshot 2026-11-05 162925](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6mG7f89ZDOsngQ8qn0yp6oxaSBtp0k8c/6de4ca581f33ee4a16eca4e83d8e77739630f9de33523613657b543040daad46.png)

![Screenshot 2026-11-05 165648](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6mG7f89ZDOsngQ8qn0yp6oxaSBtp0k8c/b428126bfd9253192a63e16cf504e1dff07a4081e8ca703d3dcc51ea4b882389.png)

 There are three separate parts:

Firstly, the bottom part. This has 4 rectangular holes in it: charge port hole, on/off switch, single pop switch, and the auto pop switch. These have text to show what they do.

![Screenshot 2026-11-05 183921](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6mG7f89ZDOsngQ8qn0yp6oxaSBtp0k8c/b571e48a045f60760d733075d93092d958210747f24632e02925e15ab1ce7fc0.png)

Inside the bottom part, there are 4 pillars with servo mounts on them. There is enough space for them to move and not hit the wall. When all 4 servos are pointing up, the plate should move up too.

![Screenshot 2026-11-05 184207](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6mG7f89ZDOsngQ8qn0yp6oxaSBtp0k8c/cc66d79120c4f4a75670d56c96722d7ebdff031f3b85c976f2da73d9fc5b8ec5.png)

There are also convenient holes on each one to guide the wires down to the nano.

The other two parts are the top popper piece which will keep the dice from popping right out of the container, and the popper plate where the dice will sit.

![Screenshot 2026-11-05 184249](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6mG7f89ZDOsngQ8qn0yp6oxaSBtp0k8c/a3c69732207a37c44dcf674add9d00e6ca6f75da953e306ddceacbd40e015975.png)

![Screenshot 2026-11-05 184251](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6mG7f89ZDOsngQ8qn0yp6oxaSBtp0k8c/d8ee5135f6456d33e3feb0e8a319259b40bd251f6d32c0c7b54a56835df90b22.png)

I used a schematic of a servo to base my mounts off of. I had to iterate a lot to get it looking and functioning (in theory) well.

### 2026-11-06: In this session, I filled up the BOM, including some parts that I already have but need to list. I also added a lot of info to the README on my github repo for this project. I started thinking about h

**2h**

In this session, I filled up the BOM, including some parts that I already have but need to list. I also added a lot of info to the README on my github repo for this project. I started thinking about how I was going to be coding the project and thought that it would probably be a good idea to have a push button instead of a switch for the single pop. I redesigned the bottom case to fit a push button that I found on Jaycar's website.

![BottomCase](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6mG7f89ZDOsngQ8qn0yp6oxaSBtp0k8c/a7a07268355958f43207c628208fb93d25d81b56e53d9edf57c9955948b88e2b.png)

I wrote up how I am going to be routing the parts. I will be using so many digital pins in this project XD.

![Screenshot 2026-11-07 103159](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6mG7f89ZDOsngQ8qn0yp6oxaSBtp0k8c/adf27022532de68d9a969d06787ff33ba081efcd56fa936d72b519c3a24e3ecb.png)
